releaseNotes: gates/ and machine/ — the 61 scripts/check-*.ts validators are split by what they grade, not by the flag they happen to take. gates/ grades a business launch and mirrors the playbook domains (gates/store/, gates/money/, gates/process/ ... 13 folders, 55 files); machine/ grades the skill itself (6 files: package parity, skill version, version discipline, source registry, reference byte budgets, and the SKILL.md autopilot contract). Both sets moved in one commit so that no validator is relocated twice when the rest of machine/ lands in the next step.

The five genuinely ambiguous gates went to gates/, not machine/. check:asc-command-contract, check:motion-contract, check:artifact-templates, check:app-archetype and check:archetype-starter all run against the skill root, which argues machine/ — but the deciding test is the SUBJECT of the assertion, not the root flag it takes. Each of their subjects is the launch: motion-contract governs the numbers a launched app animates with, asc-command-contract the commands a submission runs, app-archetype and archetype-starter the scaffold a business is built from. They exist to protect a launch, so they are gates.

gates/ mirrors the playbook domains rather than staying flat, which is what ARCHITECTURE.md already committed to. The two machine consumers of these paths are indifferent to the choice — the audit runner resolves steps by npm script name and the fixture harness by basename — so the decision rests entirely on the reader who orients before grepping, and 55 files in one directory give that reader nothing. Genuinely cross-cutting gates go to gates/process/ rather than a top-level exception bucket, because ARCHITECTURE.md already describes process/ as the cross-cutting launch-method domain; that keeps it to one placement rule instead of two.

Three gates would have gone silently dead in this move. tsconfig.json and the prettier lint:format and format globs in BOTH package manifests named scripts/**/*.ts only, so after the move the typecheck barrier and the format check would each have covered zero of the 61 moved files while the audit still reported 70 ok — the typecheck whose whole job is catching these 72 rewritten imports would have been checking nothing. check-package-parity's launchbench cross-check was the third: its scripts/ regex would not have errored, it would have stopped MATCHING, leaving basename undefined and skipping every validator while still exiting 0.

Directory assumptions are now a resolver, not a string. scripts/lib/script-paths.ts indexes gates/, machine/ and scripts/ and resolves a spawnable script by basename, throwing on an unknown or ambiguous name. The fixture harness needed this regardless of layout: it is passed bare basenames, and 7 of them (probe-posthog, probe-revenuecat, render-launch-cockpit, run-agent-evals, validate-project-state, validate-state, grade-screenshots) point at scripts that stay put, so no single hardcoded directory could have worked. The throw is the point — a wrong path exits non-zero and roughly 700 fixtures assert exit 1, so a silent fallback would turn the suite green while testing nothing. version.ts had the same bug on its design:version path, which is not an audit-plan step and so would have stayed broken behind a green audit.

An unparseable validator command is now an error with its own fixture. The old code reached continue when a command did not name a .ts file, which is exactly how a path assumption could quietly disable the cross-check; package_parity.launchbench_validator_unparseable makes it loud, and repo-gates.fixtures.ts proves it fails. The fixture count moves from 716 to 717 for that one added failing-path assertion.

Two depth idioms were invisible to a path-shaped search and are recorded here because the next migration step will meet them again: check-revenue.ts and check-attribution-contract.ts resolve the skill root inline from import.meta.url rather than through the shared scriptDir constant, and one of them uses new URL(...).pathname instead of fileURLToPath. Grepping for scriptDir found 17 of the 19 script-dir-relative resolutions; the remaining two were found only by resolving every candidate against the filesystem.
